definition: Rationed means strictly controlled and capped how much of something in short supply each person could receive, as governments do with food or fuel during a shortage or war.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rationed. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rationed should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Rationed means strictly controlled and capped how much of something in short supply each person could receive — as when wartime governments rationed gasoline and sugar, issuing coupon books that fixed every family's weekly share.
Portioned just means divided into servings, with no scarcity implied — rationed adds strict caps forced by a shortage.
Withheld goes further than rationed: a rationed supply is still handed out in small shares, but a withheld one isn't given out at all.

Allotted means given out as a fixed share — each speaker's allotted ten minutes, an allotted plot of land. It is neutral bookkeeping: shares assigned, no crisis implied. Rationed means shares were capped because supply ran short. Time is allotted at every meeting; food is rationed only in a shortage.

Apportioned means divided among parties according to some rule of fairness — costs apportioned among partners, seats apportioned by population. The focus is the formula for splitting. Rationed focuses on scarcity: a supply too small for normal use, doled out in strict, capped shares until it stretches.

Restricted means held within strict bounds — restricted access, a restricted diet. It limits use without necessarily handing anything out. Rationed is restriction plus distribution: the scarce supply is still given to everyone, just in fixed, capped shares. A restricted door stays shut; rationed bread still reaches each table.

When the blizzard pinned the climbers in their tents for a week, the expedition leader rationed the remaining food, doling out one energy bar per person each morning.
The leader strictly controlled a supply that was running short — fixed, small shares handed out on a schedule.
The one-bar-per-person rule is exactly the kind of hard cap that rationed describes.
Rationed appears constantly in writing about wars, shortages, and expeditions — governments ration fuel, ships ration fresh water.
You can also use it lightly ('I rationed my Halloween candy through November'), and the noun form is a ration: the fixed share itself.
